subject: science
intro: Nuclear processes change the nucleus of an atom and release large amounts of energy. In fission, a large nucleus splits into smaller nuclei. In fusion, small nuclei join to form a larger nucleus; fusion powers the Sun. In radioactive decay, an unstable nucleus gives off particles or energy and changes into a different nucleus over time. All of these change the composition of the nucleus and release far more energy than ordinary chemical reactions.

items.prompt: What happens to the nucleus in nuclear fission?

steps: In fission, a large nucleus splits into smaller nuclei.
This change in the nucleus releases a large amount of energy.
solution.answer: A large nucleus splits into smaller nuclei, releasing a large amount of energy.

items.prompt: What happens to nuclei in nuclear fusion, and where does this occur naturally?

steps: In fusion, small nuclei join to form a larger nucleus, releasing energy.
Fusion occurs naturally in the Sun, which is powered by fusion.
solution.answer: Small nuclei join into a larger nucleus, releasing energy; this powers the Sun.

steps: In radioactive decay, an unstable nucleus gives off particles or energy.
This changes it into a different nucleus over time.
solution.answer: When an unstable nucleus gives off particles or energy and changes into a different nucleus over time.

items.prompt: Do nuclear processes release more or less energy than ordinary chemical reactions?

steps: Nuclear processes change the nucleus itself.
They release far more energy than ordinary chemical reactions.

items.prompt: Compare fission and fusion in terms of what happens to the nuclei.

steps: Both change the composition of nuclei but in opposite ways.
Fission splits a large nucleus into smaller ones.
Fusion joins small nuclei into a larger one, so they are opposite processes.
solution.answer: Fission splits a large nucleus into smaller nuclei; fusion joins small nuclei into a larger one.

items.prompt: A model shows an unstable nucleus emitting a particle and becoming a new element. Which nuclear process is this, and what does it illustrate?

steps: Emitting a particle and becoming a new nucleus describes a specific process.
This is radioactive decay, in which an unstable nucleus changes into a different one.
The model illustrates that decay changes the nucleus's composition and releases energy.
solution.answer: Radioactive decay; the model shows the nucleus changing composition into a new element and releasing energy.
